sentences.text: Iguanodon was a large, bulky plant-eater that could grow to lengths of 9 to 11 meters and weigh as much as 4.5 metric tons.
These animals were capable of shifting between bipedal and quadrupedal locomotion depending on the situation.
Mantell compared the toothless, scoop-shaped front of its lower jaw to that of two-toed sloths and the extinct ground sloth Mylodon.
It is one of the three genera on which the name Dinosauria was originally based, alongside Megalosaurus and Hylaeosaurus.
Benjamin Waterhouse Hawkins held a banquet for twenty people inside his standing Iguanodon sculpture before it was finished.
Its top speed on two legs has been estimated at 24 km/h, and it could not gallop on all fours.
Scientists processed bones from a specimen in 2003 and successfully found identifiable proteins like phosphoproteins and proteoglycans within a rib.
The genus name was established in 1825 by the English geologist Gideon Mantell after examining fossils discovered in England.
A popular story says Mary Ann Mantell found the first teeth in Tilgate Forest in 1822, but Gideon Mantell's own accounts contradict each other, so who found them is uncertain.
By 1849, Mantell realized the animal had slender front limbs rather than the heavy, elephant-like build previously assumed.
A specific specimen from Maidstone, known as the Mantel-piece and cataloged as NHMUK 3741, was later removed from the genus Iguanodon.
With a straight tail and back, the dinosaur likely kept its body horizontal to the ground, using its arms for support when needed.
The species I. bernissartensis is famous for many skeletons found in the Sainte-Barbe Clays Formation at Bernissart, with extra remains discovered across Europe.
The massive size of the largest species allowed it to reach food growing 4 to 5 meters high in trees.
David Norman proposed that their diet consisted of horsetails, cycads, and conifers.
Iguanodontians in general have also been linked to the rise of flowering plants during the Cretaceous, although the evidence is not conclusive.
At Nehden, in Germany, a site with individuals of many ages, some of them I. bernissartensis, may record animals that lived in groups.
New analyses of the Bernissart site indicate at least three high-mortality events happened over a brief period of 10 to 100 years, though this does not prove herd living.
Research published in 2026 challenges the traditional view of an animal that switched between two and four legs, interpreting I. bernissartensis as likely an obligate quadruped.
A 2026 study provided new information regarding the variability of skull shapes in Iguanodon.
One fossil specimen shows evidence of a fractured hip bone and an injury to the ischium.
Two other individuals exhibited osteoarthritis, indicated by bone overgrowths known as osteophytes in their anklebones.
Iguanodon belongs to the larger group Iguanodontia, which also includes duck-billed hadrosaurs.
Iguanodon lived during the late Early Cretaceous, between 126 and 120 million years ago, in what is now Europe.
Dollo's reconstruction of Iguanodon with a bent tail is now considered inaccurate, as ossified tendons show that the tail was straight.
The exact function of Iguanodon thumb spikes is debated, with hypotheses suggesting they were used for defense or foraging.
In 2026, Rotatori and colleagues argued that Delapparentia is a distinct taxon related to Magnamanus and I. galvensis, a species that would need a genus name of its own.
